title: Maxwell common definitions
description: Shared building blocks referenced by every Maxwell schema. Documents never validate against this file directly

schemaVersion.description: Major version of the Maxwell document schema family. Bumped only on breaking changes

slug.description: Human-chosen identifier for companies, applications, vendors, repos, images, environments and KPIs

kpiId.description: Identifier of one of the six Maxwell KPIs. Fixed vocabulary; kpis/data/<kpiId>/ and kpis/measurement/<kpiId>.md are named after it and kpi/registry, kpi/datapoint, kpi/run and the methodology frontmatter all reference this list

eventId.description: Sequential event id within one change-management timeline: evt_1, evt_2, ... in append order

runId.description: Identifier of one headless run (a bundle of harness sessions). Set via MAXWELL_RUN_ID

sessionId.description: Harness session identifier. Claude Code uses UUIDs; OpenCode uses ses_ prefixed ids

controlId.description: Control identifier as published by the framework, e.g. SEBI CSCRF 'GV.SC.S5', ISO 'A.8.8', NIST CSF 'PR.AA-01'

weeklyWindow.description: A recurring weekly window expressed in UTC. A window whose endUtc is earlier than startUtc wraps past midnight; startUtc equal to endUtc means the whole day. Shared by application/environment allowedWindows and mirrored (with a note) by company/sdlc-policy deploymentWindow

daysOfWeek.description: Days on which the window applies

ociDigest.description: Content-addressable OCI manifest digest: 'sha256:' followed by 64 lowercase hex characters

ociReference.description: Fully-qualified OCI distribution reference: host[:port]/path[:tag][@sha256:hex]. The host must contain a dot or a port (or be localhost) so that registry-less shorthands such as node:22 or org/repo:1.0 are rejected; normalise them to docker.io/library/node:22 and docker.io/org/repo:1.0 before writing

gitUrl.description: Git remote URL: https://, ssh:// or scp-like git@host:path, optional .git suffix, no embedded credentials or traversal. Shared by application/repo and any schema that cites a repository

workspacePath.description: Path relative to the workspace root, POSIX separators, no traversal

absolutePath.description: Absolute POSIX path (leading slash, no traversal segments). Used where a harness reports a machine-local location such as its working directory

phoneE164.description: E.164 phone number: plus sign, country code and digits only

credentialKey.description: Stable handle of an entry in applications/<app_id>/credentials.json (lowercase, starts with a letter, 3-64 characters). Referenced by environment probeAccess.credentialKey, metastore catalog endpointRef and workflows; never a URL and never a secret value

contactRole.description: Closed list of governance roles a contact can hold. ceo is the MD/CEO who receives RBI board-level reporting; designated-officer is the SEBI CSCRF designated officer and the CERT-In Directions 2022 point of contact for incident reporting; grievance-officer is the DPDP Rules 2025 grievance officer; dpo is the data protection officer; the remaining roles are IT governance, audit and compliance functions

vulnId.description: Vulnerability identifier as issued by its database. CVE and GHSA ids are checked strictly; any other OSV-style id is accepted as a prefix plus dash-separated segments that may contain ':' or '.' (PYSEC-2021-123, GO-2024-2687, RHSA-2024:1892, openSUSE-SU-2024:14017-1, CGA-8crc-r3gg-jr73, UBUNTU-CVE-2022-3169, BIT-golang-2023-45288). Shared by cve/record, cve/search and soc findings

cvssVector.description: CVSS vector string with optional CVSS:<major>.<minor>/ prefix, e.g. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N or CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/U:Amber (CVSS 4.0 supplemental Provider Urgency values Clear, Green, Amber and Red are allowed). Shared by cve/record cvss.vector and soc finding.cvss.vector, which additionally require the version prefix

mitreTechniqueId.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique or sub-technique id (T1195.002) or MITRE ATLAS technique id (AML.T0010)

severity.description: Maxwell canonical severity. Map CVSS 4.0/3.1 qualitative ratings 1:1; 'info' is for observations with no risk

genAiProvider.description: Generative-AI provider name: the OpenTelemetry gen_ai.provider.name well-known values plus 'other'. Claude Code sessions are 'anthropic' unless CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK or CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX is set; OpenCode supplies providerID. session/summary models[].provider and vocab/pricing models[].provider both use this list so cost lookups join on it

modelId.description: Model identifier as the harness requested it (gen_ai.request.model), e.g. 'claude-opus-5' or 'claude-haiku-4-5'; also the shape of vocab/pricing aliases so session usage joins the price table

secretStore.description: Where secrets live. Union of the stores an environment can run against (application/environment secretsBackend) and the stores a policy may mandate (company/sdlc-policy secretsManagement.backend), so probe-sdlc compares the two by string equality; application/credentials entry.provider adds the locator kinds env and file on top of this list

actor.description: Who performed an action: a harness agent, a human, or a script

id.description: Agent name (e.g. 'iac-auditor'), human email or handle, or script path

owner.description: Accountable party: a full actor object, or simply the human's email

provenance.description: How and by whom a document or record was produced. Links outputs to harness sessions for KPI attribution

inputsHash.description: sha256 over the ordered inputs that produced this artefact, for reproducibility checks

regulatoryRef.description: Pointer to a clause or control in a regulatory instrument or framework

evidenceRef.description: Reference to evidence stored in the workspace or an external system

ref.description: Workspace path, URL, ticket key, PR URL or commit hash depending on type

assetRef.description: Points at an asset in the workspace: an application, an environment, a repo, an image, a vendor or the company itself. appId is required for application, environment, repo and image (with envId, repoId or imageId respectively); vendorId is required for vendor; company needs no id beyond the enclosing document
